note: Web bundle 13 - the scroll fix, and double-tap for read-aloud (Joshua's rulings, 2026-11-01). JOB 1 (scroll fighting): bundle 12's own phone reports showed a drag that counted 110 touchmoves and moved the container not at all, and another that leapt ~6,676 px. Harness traces against the real app found the causes in the gesture layer, not in the saved place (zero rendition.display calls during or after drags; the save path only ever saves): (i) the hand-walk measured the finger in clientY inside a section document - a coordinate whose origin the walk itself moves as the container scrolls, so the walk could be fed its own output (stall in one book, oscillation in another); the walk now measures Touch.screenY, which no scroll can move. (ii) The release fling's velocity was smoothed from the last move samples, so a duplicated/out-of-order final sample flipped the fling and carried the reader back to the drag's exact start (reproduced to the pixel: 796 -> 795); velocity now comes from the drag's net displacement over its trailing window. (iii) New guards: a move delivery that exactly repeats an earlier position of the same touch is a stale replay and is dropped whole, one walk step is capped at 120 px, and the fling at 3 px/ms. The drag probe is extended: a passive trap counts programmatic scrollTop sets in the 1 s after a drag ends, tagged by caller (gesture / epub-display / epub-scroll / audit / other), and a follow-up report always sends - zero is the proof. Position saving is unchanged. JOB 2 (gestures): double-tap on the page or the edge zones now toggles read-aloud; press-and-hold no longer starts it (the binding is removed entirely - a hold is inert). A gate inside fireTap holds a single tap for a 300 ms double-tap window and discards it when a second tap lands, so a double-tap turns ZERO pages; harness-proven (single tap = 1 turn, double-tap = 0 turns + reader toggle, long-press = nothing). Single tap on a marked (blue) term still floats its definition in place, undelayed (it travels the click path, not the held tap path); a double-tap starting on a term dismisses the card and yields to the reader. A double-tap on a picture keeps the picture (first tap opens it, as before) and does not start the reader. Single taps on page/zones now act 300 ms after the tap - the measured cost of the double-tap window; the definition pop-up does not pay it. The automatic reader's toast now says 'double-tap again to stop'. Not in this bundle, honestly: tap-and-hold on an ordinary word for a dictionary lookup cannot ship in a web bundle - the shell bridge has no dictionary method and no ColorDict/GoldenDict intent exists in the app. What serves tapping a word today is the books' own marked-term definitions (the in-place pop-up). The doorway needs a shell change (a ReaderBridge dictionary method plus web-side word capture); bundle 13 leaves long-press unbound so the gesture is free for it. Full evidence: BUNDLE13-REPORT.md.
